rules.tract: Find the root tract, meaning pull or draw
rules.ed: Add -ed to form to tell about the past
rules.un: Add un- to informed to mean not informed

ruleHelp.tract: Read each whole word. Tractor, extract, attract, retract, distract and traction share tract; do not treat tract as the base word for every word.
ruleHelp.form: Inform, formal, uniform and misinform contain form. Read the whole word; mis- means wrongly in misinform.
ruleHelp.ed: form → formed: keep form and add ed.
ruleHelp.un: informed → uninformed: un- means not; keep informed after the prefix.

vocab.title: Because of Winn-Dixie
vocab.groupsNote: Study all 12 words: the teacher will choose 6 at random on Nov 13. Teacher definitions are copied exactly. Parent note: the printed definition for Distracted appears mismatched; confirm it with the teacher. In ordinary use, distracted means having your attention pulled away.

words.sentence: The market sells produce such as apples and carrots.
words.fill: We put fresh ___, including lettuce and peaches, into our basket.

words.def: A case where a rule does not apply
words.sentence: The guide dog was an exception to the store’s no-pets rule.
words.fill: A rule applies to everyone except one special case called an ___.

words.def: When money is paid over a length of time
words.sentence: The family paid one installment each month until the bicycle was paid for.
words.fill: Each scheduled payment toward the full cost is an ___.

words.sentence: A purple carrot looked peculiar beside the orange carrots.
An employee at the market stacked fruit during her paid shift.
words.fill: A person who works for pay is an ___.

words.def: favored by or involving good luck or fortune
words.sentence: We were fortunate that the rain stopped before our picnic.
words.fill: Having good luck made us feel ___.

words.def: lacking knowledge or awareness in general
words.sentence: I was ignorant about constellations before I studied the stars.
words.fill: Before learning the rules, I was ___ about how the game worked.

words.sentence: The sad music filled the room with melancholy.
words.fill: The story’s sad ending left a feeling of ___.

words.sentence: My trustworthy teammate kept his promise to return the ball.
words.fill: Because she always keeps her promises, she is ___.

words.def: A group of stars in the night sky that make up a picture or a pattern
words.sentence: We spotted constellations that formed patterns in the night sky.
words.fill: Groups of stars that appear to form pictures are ___.

words.sentence: The irritating tapping made it hard to enjoy the story.
words.fill: The repeated squeak was ___ because it kept bothering us.

words.def: To prevent something from continuing as usual
words.sentence: I was distracted by a butterfly while I was reading.
words.fill: My attention moved away from my book, so I became ___.
words.note: The printed definition appears mismatched. In ordinary use, distracted means having your attention pulled away. Confirm the class-sheet definition with the teacher.

words.def: The denominator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are in the whole. It is the bottom part of the fraction
A unit fraction is ONE part of a whole. It always has a numerator of one.
The numerator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are being described. It is the top part of the fraction.
A fraction is a number used when a whole is split into equal parts.
